purpose: Test whether the Stage 2 activation ranking transfers to a dense-connectivity backbone without reopening the superseded transfer panel.
connectivity: feature concatenation rather than residual addition
activation_site_policy: independent modules plus an explicit replaceable final activation
selection_rationale: LGTS-f4-Alpha was selected after the completed Stage 1 component ablation using macro-F1, paired seed differences, average rank and the simplicity principle. The remaining activations are the locked structural and classical controls from Stage 2.
duplicate_policy: No explicit ReLU condition is included because DenseNet121 Native is ReLU at the same replaceable activation sites.

training.batch_size_rationale: DenseNet121 full-backbone LGTS at batch 128 saturated the 24 GB GPU and triggered WDDM shared-memory thrashing before the first completed epoch. Batch 64 was locked before any Stage 3 result was produced and is held constant for every activation and seed.

runtime_acceleration.rationale: TF32 and deterministic cuDNN kernel benchmarking were locked before any completed Stage 3 run. channels-last was rejected during a pre-result timing check because it was slower for DenseNet121 with 64x64 inputs and the custom full-backbone activation. performance_mode remains disabled.

test_policy: Official test partitions remain sealed during validation-based model selection.
resume_policy: Each activation-seed condition runs in a fresh Python process; completed conditions are skipped and an interrupted condition restarts from epoch 1. A named mutex prevents duplicate launchers.
supersedes_for_future_execution: The unfinished 465-run legacy transfer panel and 220-run legacy DenseNet121 panel are retained as historical artifacts but are not resumed.
